html:
In a referendum held over 29 June and 1 July 1984, the men of Liechtenstein voted narrowly to give women the right to vote in national elections. It was the last country in Europe to do so.

Earlier referendums in 1971 and 1973 had failed. Like Switzerland, Liechtenstein gave the decision to male voters themselves, which slowed the change.

The result passed with just over half the votes. Women first voted in 1986. The case is often set beside Finland, which gave women the vote eighty years earlier, as a sign of how late reform came in parts of the Alps. See the principality.
